title: Start with failure boundaries and business impact
points: Map component, Availability Zone, Region, account and data-corruption failures to user impact. Define business continuity requirements before selecting a recovery technology.
layout: glossy architecture diagram with thin glass panels

title: RPO and RTO are different clocks
points: RPO is maximum tolerable data loss measured back from incident; RTO is maximum tolerable service restoration time. Show two time axes and recovery evidence.
layout: glossy architecture diagram with thin glass panels

title: Choose the DR posture by target
points: Compare backup and restore, pilot light, warm standby and active-active across standing capacity, operational complexity, RPO and RTO. No invented universal durations.
layout: glossy architecture diagram with thin glass panels

title: Backup and restore rebuilds the environment
points: Cross-Region/cross-account recovery points plus infrastructure as code, AMIs, configuration and secrets. During disaster, restore data and deploy application before traffic cutover.
layout: glossy architecture diagram with thin glass panels

title: Pilot light keeps the data core alive
points: Replicate core data and minimal services to recovery Region; scale application and supporting capacity on failover. Pre-test quotas, launch templates and dependencies.
layout: glossy architecture diagram with thin glass panels

title: Warm standby serves at reduced capacity
points: Maintain a functional secondary Region at smaller scale; expand capacity and redirect traffic on incident. Test scaling, data replication and endpoint health.
layout: glossy architecture diagram with thin glass panels

title: Active-active needs conflict decisions
points: Both Regions serve traffic; route users and define write ownership, consistency, conflict resolution and failback. Active-active increases resilience and complexity.
layout: glossy architecture diagram with thin glass panels

title: Continuous server recovery with AWS DRS
points: AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery continuously replicates block changes into a low-cost staging area; launch recovery instances for drill or failover, validate and plan failback.
layout: glossy architecture diagram with thin glass panels

title: AWS DRS drill and failback walkthrough
points: Configure source agents and launch settings, monitor replication, perform non-disruptive recovery drill, test application and DNS, then exercise controlled failback.
layout: glossy architecture diagram with thin glass panels

title: A backup is useful only after a restore test
points: Schedule recovery points, restore into isolated environment, validate data and application, measure RPO/RTO, record evidence and close gaps. Backup job success is insufficient.
layout: glossy architecture diagram with thin glass panels

title: Centralize backup policy across accounts
points: AWS Organizations backup policies, AWS Backup plans, vaults, cross-account/cross-Region copies and audit controls. Distinguish policy assignment from successful protected resources.
layout: glossy architecture diagram with thin glass panels

title: Design retention from recovery needs
points: Select backup frequency, lifecycle and retention by RPO, compliance and cost. Restore points and legal hold/immutability are separate controls.
layout: glossy architecture diagram with thin glass panels

title: Protect recovery points from tampering
points: S3 Object Lock, EBS snapshot lock and AWS Backup Vault Lock protect against unauthorized deletion or shortening retention according to configured mode and scope. Test restore access.
layout: glossy architecture diagram with thin glass panels

title: Replication can spread corruption
points: Asynchronous copy reduces lag but can propagate erroneous writes/deletes. Pair replication with versioning, point-in-time recovery and immutable recovery points.
layout: glossy architecture diagram with thin glass panels

title: Database recovery varies by service
points: RDS/Aurora snapshots and PITR, DynamoDB PITR/global tables, S3 versioning/replication. Compare restoration target, consistency and cross-Region prerequisites.
layout: glossy architecture diagram with thin glass panels

title: Route 53 health checks and failover
points: Use health checks and failover routing to select healthy endpoints; DNS TTL and client caches affect switch time. Test recovery endpoint and dependency health.
layout: glossy architecture diagram with thin glass panels

title: Global Accelerator changes traffic quickly
points: Anycast static IPs and endpoint health steer new flows to healthy endpoints; application data, session and Regional capacity must already be ready.
layout: glossy architecture diagram with thin glass panels

title: ARC routing controls govern failover
points: Amazon Application Recovery Controller routing controls and safety rules coordinate recovery state across Regions. Prefer preprovisioned data-plane controls during disruption.
layout: glossy architecture diagram with thin glass panels

title: ARC zonal shift is a different boundary
points: Zonal shift moves supported load-balanced traffic away from an impaired AZ; it does not replace Regional disaster recovery or repair underlying data.
layout: glossy architecture diagram with thin glass panels

title: Multi-cluster containers need data recovery too
points: ECS/EKS clusters in separate Regions need images, manifests, secrets, networking, capacity and data replication. Traffic shift succeeds only with healthy dependencies.
layout: glossy architecture diagram with thin glass panels

title: Resilience Hub finds recovery gaps
points: Define application and resilience policy, assess estimated RTO/RPO, examine recommendations, implement changes, then reassess and run tests. Estimate is not measured recovery.
layout: glossy architecture diagram with thin glass panels

title: Runbooks turn a plan into repeatable action
points: Systems Manager Automation documents coordinate approved recovery steps, validation and rollback; include permissions, parameter checks, human gates and evidence.
layout: glossy architecture diagram with thin glass panels

title: Fault injection tests the hypothesis
points: AWS Fault Injection Service experiment template sets controlled target, action, stop conditions and monitoring; establish steady state, inject failure, observe and restore.
layout: glossy architecture diagram with thin glass panels

title: Measure the drill, not the diagram
points: Time detection, declaration, automation, data recovery and traffic restoration; measure actual data-loss point and user outcome against RTO/RPO.
layout: glossy architecture diagram with thin glass panels

title: Walkthrough: recover a failed Region
points: Detect Region failure, activate ARC routing control or traffic policy, verify secondary data and capacity, shift traffic, validate user journeys and record recovery metrics.
layout: glossy architecture diagram with thin glass panels

title: Walkthrough: restore after ransomware
points: Contain compromised identity, select clean immutable recovery point, restore in isolated account/Region, validate integrity, rotate secrets and return traffic after approval.
layout: glossy architecture diagram with thin glass panels

title: Choose the recovery mechanism
points: Decision table: periodic restore -> Backup; server block replication -> DRS; health-based DNS -> Route 53; preprovisioned traffic control -> ARC; resilience assessment -> Resilience Hub; controlled faults -> FIS.
layout: glossy architecture diagram with thin glass panels

title: Recovery readiness checklist
points: Table of objectives, protection, isolation, immutable copies, IaC, quotas, runbooks, test results, ownership, failback and evidence. Remember: a rehearsed recovery path is an architecture component.
layout: glossy architecture diagram with thin glass panels
